system_description.narrative_title: Multipolar Turbulence: War, Energy Shocks and Bond Stress
system_description.narrative_summary: The global geopolitical order is an open, tightly coupled system under stress from simultaneous security shocks (Russia–Ukraine escalation, Iran-region attacks, Yemen/Houthi strikes), an energy-and-shipping squeeze, and a broad sovereign bond-market rout. Electoral and domestic political dynamics—especially in the US and key European states—are shortening policy time horizons and amplifying volatile feedbacks between markets, supply chains and military risk. The result is heightened fragility: local crises cascade through energy flows and financial markets, forcing ad hoc policy interventions that reshape alliance behaviour and economic activity in real time.
system_description.scope: State and alliance interactions, regional conflict theatres (Eastern Europe, Middle East, Horn of Africa), global energy and maritime routes, international financial markets (sovereign bond markets, liquidity), multinational corporations and critical supply chains, and the domestic political dynamics that drive policy choices.
system_description.super_system: The planetary socio-economic-political-technical system: the globalized economy, international institutions and security architectures embedded in the Earth's ecological and information environment.
adjacent_subsystems: Global energy and maritime security (Strait of Hormuz, Red Sea, tanker flows and refining capacity)
International financial markets and sovereign debt dynamics (bond yields, Eurozone stress, liquidity)
Europe–Russia regional security complex (NATO relations, intelligence/espionage, eastern flank posture)

variables.name: Russia-Ukraine war
variables.description: An ongoing large-scale conflict between Russia and Ukraine driven by renewed Russian strikes and offensives that are shifting front lines and military dynamics in Europe.

variables.name: Iran-linked Middle East escalation
variables.description: Iran and allied proxies (notably Yemen's Houthis) are intensifying attacks on shipping and regional targets, threatening maritime routes through the Strait of Hormuz and amplifying Gulf security risks.

variables.name: U.S.-China tech and trade rivalry
variables.description: The United States and China are contesting technology, trade and investment regimes—via export controls, data-security measures and market-access battles—that are restructuring global supply chains and standards.

variables.name: France sovereign debt and bond-market stress
variables.description: France's fiscal strain and surging sovereign bond yields are constraining policy choices, provoking market-driven pressure on public finances and raising contagion concerns for European financial stability.

variables.name: Germany industrial and auto-sector transition
variables.description: Germany's industrial and automotive sectors are undergoing a structural shift toward electrification, automation and new production models, challenging legacy manufacturers and national industrial strategy.
